info.bio:
Gang Green (also spelled GangGreen) is a hardcore punk/crossover thrash band originally from Braintree, Massachusetts. The first incarnation of the band consisted of 15 year olds Chris Doherty, Mike Dean, and Bill Manley and contributed seven tracks to the This Is Boston, Not L.A. compilation in 1982. That same year the group disbanded and lead singer Chris Doherty joined the band Jerry's Kids for their album Is This My World?

Current line-up:
Chris Doherty – Vocals, Guitar (July 1980 – present)

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: Boston Area Indie Band
podcast.body: Gang Green is listed as one of the amazing indie bands that emerged from the Boston area's rich college music scene. "We had Mission of Burma, the Delphwegos, the Lemonheads, Gang Green, the throwing muses, Dinosaur, Junior, Julianne Hatfield and the Blake Babies, and of course the greatest Boston area college band of them all, the Pixies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Lifestyle Choice
podcast.body: Unlike some straight-edge hardcore bands, Gang Green was known for members who embraced drugs and alcohol. "Other groups kind of liked their drugs and alcohol, and that included the very fierce gang green."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rejection of Straight Edge Philosophy
podcast.body: Unlike some Boston hardcore bands influenced by Ian MacKaye's straight edge philosophy, Gang Green was an example of a group that embraced drugs and alcohol. They were known for their fierce approach, in contrast to the "Boston Crew" who policed shows. "Other groups kind of liked their drugs and alcohol. And that included the very fierce gang green."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Physical Manifestations of Illness (1998)
xref.body: By 1998, there were rumors that Lane Staley had contracted gangrene from continuous needle use and had stopped eating due to rotting teeth, only being able to consume protein drinks designed for seniors. "By 1998, there were more rumors that he had contracted gang green from nonstop needle use, that he'd stopped eating because his teeth were rotting out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
